verses.english_translation: He who, seated like one unconcerned, is not moved by the Gunas, who, knowing that the Gunas operate, is self-centered and remains firm.

essence.reflection: Stability comes from realizing 'I am not doing this.' Let the world spin; you stay at the center.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
समदुःखसुखः स्वस्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ।
तुल्यप्रियाप्रियो धीरस्तुल्यनिन्दात्मसंस्तुतिः
verses.english_translation: Balanced in pleasure and pain, self-abiding, viewing a clod of earth, a stone, and gold alike; the same to agreeable and disagreeable, firm, the same in censure and praise.

essence.reflection: When you are established in yourself, gold and dirt have the same value because neither can add to or subtract from your completeness.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मानापमानयोस्तुल्यस्तुल्यो मित्रारिपक्षयोः ।
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी गुणातीतः स उच्यते
verses.english_translation: The same in honor and disgrace, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings—he is said to have crossed the Gunas.

essence.reflection: To transcend nature, stop trying to conquer it with your ego. Let go of the sense of 'I am starting this project'.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मां च योऽव्यभिचारेण भक्तियोगेन सेवते ।
स गुणान्समतीत्यैतान्ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते
verses.english_translation: And he who serves Me with unswerving devotion, he, crossing beyond the Gunas, is fit for becoming Brahman.

essence.reflection: Bhakti is the rocket fuel that blasts you out of the gravitational pull of the Gunas. Love for God conquers nature.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रतिष्ठाहममृतस्याव्ययस्य च ।
शाश्वतस्य च धर्मस्य सुखस्यैकान्तिकस्य च
verses.english_translation: For I am the Abode of Brahman, the Immortal and Immutable, of everlasting Dharma and of Absolute Bliss.

essence.reflection: Krishna reveals the ultimate secret: The Personal God (Krishna) is the very foundation of the Formless Absolute (Brahman) and Eternal Bliss.

chapters.title: Purushottama Yoga
chapters.subtitle: The Yoga of the Supreme Divine Personality

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम् ।
छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्
verses.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of an imperishable Ashvattha tree, with its root above and branches below. Its leaves are the Vedic hymns. He who knows it knows the Vedas.

essence.reflection: The world is like a reflection of the Divine. The roots (Source) are in the Spirit above, while the branches (Material Life) grow downwards. Understand this structure to navigate life.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अधश्चोर्ध्वं प्रसृतास्तस्य शाखा
गुणप्रवृद्धा विषयप्रवालाः ।
अधश्च मूलान्यनुसन्ततानि
कर्मानुबन्धीनि मनुष्यलोके
verses.english_translation: Below and above spread its branches, nourished by the Gunas; sense objects are its buds; and below in the world of men stretch forth the roots, originating action.

essence.reflection: Our actions create secondary roots (vasanas) that bind us further to this world. The more we act for sensory results, the deeper we get entangled.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
न रूपमस्येह तथोपलभ्यते
नान्तो न चादिर्न च सम्प्रतिष्ठा ।
अश्वत्थमेनं सुविरूढमूल-
मसङ्गशस्त्रेण दृढेन छित्त्वा
verses.english_translation: Its form is not perceived here as such, neither its end, nor its origin, nor its foundation. Having cut asunder this firmly rooted Ashvattha tree with the strong sword of non-attachment...

essence.krishna_guidance: Cut it with the Sword of Detachment (Asanga-shastra).
essence.reflection: You cannot unravel the complexities of life; you must cut through them. Detachment is the only sharp weapon capable of severing these deep roots.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ततः पदं तत्परिमार्गितव्यं
यस्मिन्गता न निवर्तन्ति भूयः ।
तमेव चाद्यं पुरुषं प्रपद्ये ।
यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी
verses.english_translation: ...Then that Goal should be sought for, whither having gone none returns again. I seek refuge in that Primeval Purusha whence streamed forth the ancient activity (or energy).

essence.krishna_guidance: Seek the Goal of no return.
essence.reflection: Don't aim for temporary heavens. Aim for the Source itself. Resolve to find that place from which you never have to fall back into ignorance.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा
अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः ।
द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञे-
र्गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत्
verses.english_translation: Free from pride and delusion, victorious over the evil of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, their desires having completely retired, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach that Eternal Goal.

essence.krishna_guidance: Be free from Pride and Delusion.
essence.reflection: Qualifications for entry into the Eternal: No ego, no bad company, no desire, and no mood swings (dualities). Only the pure can enter.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः ।
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम
verses.english_translation: Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the fire illumines that; having gone thither, they return not; that is My Supreme Abode.

essence.reflection: The physical lights of the universe cannot reveal the Spirit. The Spirit lights Itself. Reaching there means finding your permanent home.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ममैवांशो जीवलोके जीवभूतः सनातनः ।
मनःषष्ठानीन्द्रियाणि प्रकृतिस्थानि कर्षति
verses.english_translation: An eternal portion of My own Self becomes the living soul in the world of life, and draws to itself the five senses with the mind for the sixth, abiding in Nature.

essence.krishna_guidance: Know you are My Eternal Fragment (Amsha).
essence.reflection: You are not a sinner; you are a spark of God. You are struggling because you are dragging the heavy burden of the senses and mind through Nature.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
शरीरं यवाप्नोति यच्चाप्युत्क्रामतीश्वरः ।
गृहीत्वैतानि संयाति वायुर्गन्धानिवाशयात्
verses.english_translation: When the Lord obtains a body and when He leaves it, He takes these (senses and mind) and goes, as the wind carries scents from their sources.

essence.reflection: Death is just moving house. You pack up your mental baggage (habits, desires) and carry it to the next location, just like wind carries perfume.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
श्रोत्रं चक्षुः स्पर्शनं च रसनं घ्राणमेव च ।
अधिष्ठाय मनश्चायं विषयानुपसेवते
verses.english_translation: Presiding over the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste, and the smell, and also the mind, He experiences the objects of the senses.

essence.reflection: The body is dead hardware. It is the Soul that sits inside and 'tastes' the world through the windows of the senses.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
उत्क्रामन्तं स्थितं वापि भुञ्जानं वा गुणान्वितम् ।
विमूढा नानुपश्यन्ति पश्यन्ति ज्ञानचक्षुषः
verses.english_translation: The deluded do not see Him who departs, stays, and enjoys; but they who possess the eye of knowledge behold Him.

essence.reflection: Most people are blind to the Spirit; they only see the body eating or dying. Wisdom is the ability to see the Driver inside the car.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यतन्तो योगिनश्चैनं पश्यन्त्यात्मन्यवस्थितम् ।
यतन्तोऽप्यकृतात्मानो नैनं पश्यन्त्यचेतसः
verses.english_translation: The Yogis, striving (for perfection), behold Him dwelling in themselves; but the unrefined and unintelligent, even though striving, see Him not.

essence.reflection: Effort alone is not enough; purity is required. A muddy mirror cannot reflect the sun, no matter how much you angle it.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् ।
यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम्
verses.english_translation: That light which residing in the sun illumines the whole world, that which is in the moon and in the fire—know that light to be Mine.

essence.reflection: The energy that lights up the universe—whether cosmic (sun) or domestic (fire)—is a manifestation of the Divine power.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा ।
पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः
verses.english_translation: Permeating the earth I support all beings by (My) energy; and having become the watery moon, I nourish all herbs.

essence.reflection: Gravity that holds the earth and the nutrients in your food are forms of God's care for you.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अहं वैश्वानरो भूत्वा प्राणिनां देहमाश्रितः ।
प्राणापानसमायुक्तः पचाम्यन्नं चतुर्विधम्
verses.english_translation: I, having become the fire Vaisvanara, abide in the body of living beings, and associated with Prana and Apana, digest the fourfold food.

essence.reflection: The very biological process that keeps you alive—digestion—is God performing a Yajna inside your stomach.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्टो
मत्तः स्मृतिर्ज्ञानमपोहनञ्च ।
वेदैश्च सर्वैरहमेव वेद्यो
वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्
verses.english_translation: And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me are memory, knowledge, and their absence. I am He to be known by all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas.

essence.krishna_guidance: Know Me as the Inner Controller.
essence.reflection: God is the source of your memory and intelligence. He is the goal of all study and the teacher of all truth.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ लोके क्षरश्चाक्षर एव च ।
क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते
verses.english_translation: There are two Purushas in the world: the Perishable and the Imperishable. All beings are the Perishable, and the Kutastha (immutable) is called the Imperishable.

essence.reflection: Understand the dual nature of existence: the changing forms (perishable) and the unchanging witness (imperishable).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
उत्तमः पुरुषस्त्वन्यः परमात्मेत्युदाहृतः ।
यो लोकत्रयमाविश्य बिभर्त्यव्यय ईश्वरः
verses.english_translation: But distinct is the Supreme Purusha, called the Highest Self, the Indestructible Lord, who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them.

essence.reflection: Beyond the changing world and the individual soul lies the Supreme Reality that supports both. This is God.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यस्मात्क्षरमतीतोऽहमक्षरादपि चोत्तमः ।
अतोऽस्मि लोके वेदे च प्रथितः पुरुषोत्तमः
verses.english_translation: Since I transcend the Perishable and am higher even than the Imperishable, therefore am I declared as the Purushottama (Supreme Spirit) in the world and in the Vedas.

essence.reflection: Krishna reveals his ultimate status: He is beyond both matter and individual souls. He is the Supreme Person.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यो मामेवमसम्मूढो जानाति पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
स सर्वविद्भजति मां सर्वभावेन भारत
verses.english_translation: He who, undeluded, thus knows Me as the Supreme Purusha, he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being, O Bharata.

essence.krishna_guidance: Worship Me with All Your Being.
essence.reflection: Knowing God as the Supreme Person is the 'theory of everything'. Once you know this, your entire life becomes an act of worship.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
इति गुह्यतमं शास्त्रमिदमुक्तं मयानघ ।
एतद्बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमान्स्यात्कृतकृत्यश्च भारत
verses.english_translation: Thus, this most secret science has been taught by Me, O sinless one; knowing this, a man becomes wise and all his duties are accomplished, O Bharata.

essence.reflection: This is the master key. Knowing this secret, you have achieved what you came here to achieve. Your life's mission is complete.

chapters.title: Daivasura Sampad Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.subtitle: The Yoga of Divine & Demonic Qualities

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अभयं सत्त्वसंशुद्धिर्ज्ञानयोगव्यवस्थितिः ।
दानं दमश्च यज्ञश्च स्वाध्यायस्तप आर्जवम्
verses.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: Fearlessness, purification of one's existence, cultivation of spiritual knowledge, charity, self-control, performance of sacrifice, study of the Vedas, austerity, and simplicity...

essence.reflection: The foundation of spiritual life is courage and a clean heart. These virtues are the wealth of a divine soul.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अहिंसा सत्यमक्रोधस्त्यागः शान्तिरपैशुनम् ।
दया भूतेष्वलोलुप्त्वं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम्
verses.english_translation: ...Non-violence, truthfulness, freedom from anger, renunciation, tranquillity, aversion to fault-finding, compassion for all living entities, freedom from covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and steady determination...

essence.reflection: Divine nature is soft yet strong. It includes being gentle (Mardavam) to others but firm in one's own values.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता ।
भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत
verses.english_translation: ...Vigor, forgiveness, fortitude, cleanliness, freedom from envy, and the absence of pride—these qualities, O Bharata, belong to godly men endowed with divine nature.

essence.reflection: True power (Tejas) is compatible with forgiveness (Kshama) and humility (Na-atimanita). These define a divine birth.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
दम्भो दर्पोऽभिमानश्च क्रोधः पारुष्यमेव च ।
अज्ञानं चाभिजातस्य पार्थ सम्पदमासुरीम्
verses.english_translation: Hypocrisy, arrogance, pride, anger, harshness, and ignorance—these qualities belong to those of demoniac nature, O Partha.

essence.reflection: Identify the weeds in your mental garden. Harshness and pride are signs of a spiritual decline.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
दैवी सम्पद्विमोक्षाय निबन्धायासुरी मता ।
मा शुचः सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातोऽसि पाण्डव
verses.english_translation: The divine qualities are conducive to liberation, whereas the demoniacal qualities are for bondage. Do not grieve, O Pandava, for you are born with the divine nature.

essence.reflection: Reassurance from the Divine: You have the good qualities within you. Your destiny is liberation, not bondage.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
द्वौ भूतसर्गो लोकेऽस्मिन्दैव आसुर एव च ।
दैवो विस्तरशः प्रोक्त आसुरं पार्थ मे शृणु
verses.english_translation: There are two kinds of beings in this world—the divine and the demoniac. I have described the divine at length; now hear from Me of the demoniac, O Partha.

essence.reflection: The world is a mix of these two types of people (and tendencies within us). Knowing the negative helps us avoid it.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च जना न विदुरासुराः ।
न शौचं नापि चाचारो न सत्यं तेषु विद्यते
verses.english_translation: Those of demoniac nature do not know what to do and what not to do; neither purity, nor right conduct, nor truth is found in them.

essence.reflection: The demonic mind is characterized by confusion about Right and Wrong action. It lacks the moral compass of Truth.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
असत्यमप्रतिष्ठं ते जगदाहुरनीश्वरम् ।
अपरस्परसम्भूतं किमन्यत्कामहैतुकम्
verses.english_translation: They say that this world is unreal, without a foundation, without a God, produced without causal relation, with lust for its cause; what else?

essence.reflection: Believing the universe is a random accident driven only by lust leads to a meaningless and destructive worldview.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
एतां दृष्टिमवष्टभ्य नष्टात्मानोऽल्पबुद्धयः ।
प्रभवन्त्युग्रकर्माणः क्षयाय जगतोऽहिताः
verses.english_translation: Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds come forth as the enemies of the world for its destruction.

essence.reflection: When intelligence is disconnected from divinity, it becomes 'fierce' (Ugra) and destroys the world instead of saving it.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
काममाश्रित्य दुष्पूरं दम्भमानमदान्विताः ।
मोहाद्गृहीत्वासद्ग्राहान्प्रवर्तन्तेऽशुचिव्रताः
verses.english_translation: Filled with insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride, and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they work with impure resolves.

essence.reflection: Chasing desires that can never be fulfilled leads to hypocrisy and impure lifestyle. It is a trap of delusion.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
चिन्तामपरिमेयां च प्रलयान्तामुपाश्रिताः ।
कामोपभोगपरमा एतावदिति निश्चिताः
verses.english_translation: Beset with immense cares ending only with death, regarding gratification of lust as the highest, and feeling sure that that is all...

essence.reflection: A materialistic life is an endless cycle of anxiety that ends only at death. Believing 'this is all there is' limits the soul.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
आशापाशशतैर्बद्धाः कामक्रोधपरायणाः ।
ईहन्ते कामभोगार्थमन्यायेनार्थसञ्चयान्
verses.english_translation: ...Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards of wealth for sensual enjoyment.

essence.reflection: When lust and anger drive the ambition, ethics are lost. Striving for wealth through injustice binds one in the 'noose of hope'.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
इदमद्य मया लब्धमिमं प्राप्स्ये मनोरथम् ।
इदमस्तीदमपि मे भविष्यति पुनर्धनम्
verses.english_translation: 'This has been gained by me today; this desire I shall obtain; this is mine, and this wealth also shall be mine in future.'

essence.reflection: The demonic mind is obsessed with accumulation and the 'I' concept. It constantly counts its gains and plans future conquests.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
असौ मया हतः शत्रुर्हनिष्ये चापरानपि ।
ईश्वरोऽहमहं भोगी सिद्धोऽहं बलवान्सुखी
verses.english_translation: 'That enemy has been slain by me, and others also I shall slay. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfected, powerful, and happy.'

essence.reflection: The ultimate delusion is thinking you are the controller of life and death. This arrogance ('I am Ishvara') is the peak of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
आढ्योऽभिजनवानस्मि कोऽन्योऽस्ति सदृशो मया ।
यक्ष्ये दास्यामि मोदिष्य इत्यज्ञानविमोहिताः
verses.english_translation: 'I am rich and well-born. Who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, I will give, I will rejoice.' Thus deluded by ignorance...

essence.reflection: Thinking one is unique or superior because of birth or money is a hallucination. It leads to performing rituals for show, not devotion.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अनेकचित्तविभ्रान्ता मोहजालसमावृताः ।
प्रसक्ताः कामभोगेषु पतन्ति नरकेऽशुचौ
verses.english_translation: ...Bewildered by many thoughts, entangled in the meshes of delusion, and addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.

essence.reflection: A confused mind (Aneka-chitta) leads to a chaotic life and eventually a dark destiny (Naraka).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
आत्मसम्भाविताः स्तब्धा धनमानमदान्विताः ।
यजन्ते नामयज्ञैस्ते दम्भेनाविधिपूर्वकम्
verses.english_translation: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name only, out of ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.

essence.reflection: Worship done for show (Dambha) or pride is useless. True sacrifice requires humility and adherence to proper methods.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्प कामं क्रोधं च संश्रिताः ।
मामात्मपरदेहेषु प्रद्विषन्तोऽभ्यसूयकाः
verses.english_translation: Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust, and anger, these malicious people hate Me, dwelling in their own bodies and in the bodies of others.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do not Hate the Divine within.
essence.reflection: Hating others is hating God, who dwells in everyone. Ego and anger blind us to this presence.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तानहं द्विषतः क्रूरान्संसारेषु नराधमान् ।
क्षिपाम्यजस्रमशुभानासुरीष्वेव योनिषु
verses.english_translation: These cruel haters, the worst among men in the world, I hurl these evil-doers forever into the wombs of demons only.

essence.reflection: Cruelty and hatred create a downward spiral. The consequence of acting like a demon is becoming one in future births.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
आसुरीं योनिमापन्ना मूढा जन्मनि जन्मनि ।
मामप्राप्यैव कौन्तेय ततो यान्त्यधमां गतिम्
verses.english_translation: Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded birth after birth, not attaining Me, they thus go to the lowest goal, O Kaunteya.

essence.reflection: Ignoring the Divine leads to spiritual regression. It is a warning to wake up before the habit of delusion becomes permanent.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत्
verses.english_translation: Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self—Lust, Anger, and Greed; therefore, one should abandon these three.

essence.reflection: These are the 'Three Gates of Hell'. They destroy the soul's peace and clarity. Recognizing them is the first step to closing the gates.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
एतैर्विमुक्तः कौन्तेय तमोद्वारैस्त्रिभिर्नरः ।
आचरत्यात्मनः श्रेयस्ततो याति परां गतिम्
verses.english_translation: A man who is liberated from these three gates to darkness, O son of Kunti, does what is good for his soul and thus attains the Supreme Goal.

essence.reflection: Once you step away from lust, anger, and greed, you are free to do what is truly good for you, leading to the highest destination.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यः शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य वर्तते कामकारतः ।
न स सिद्धिमवाप्नोति न सुखं न परां गतिम्
verses.english_translation: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, attains not perfection, nor happiness, nor the Supreme Goal.

essence.reflection: Ignoring wisdom traditions (Scriptures) to follow every whim leads to failure. Freedom is not doing whatever you want; it is doing what is right.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तस्माच्छास्त्रं प्रमाणं ते कार्याकार्यव्यवस्थितौ ।
ज्ञात्वा शास्त्रविधानोक्तं कर्म कर्तुमिहार्हसि
verses.english_translation: Therefore, let the scripture be the authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scripture, you should act here in this world.

essence.reflection: When in doubt, consult the wisdom of the ages. Use established ethical codes to navigate the complexities of life and duty.

chapters.title: Shraddha Traya Vibhaga Yoga
chapters.subtitle: The Yoga of the Threefold Division of Faith

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ये शास्त्रविधिमुत्सृज्य यजन्ते श्रद्धयान्विताः ।
तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः
verses.english_translation: Arjuna said: Those who, setting aside the ordinances of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith, what is their condition, O Krishna? Is it Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas?

essence.reflection: Is faith alone enough? Arjuna inquires if sincerity validates an action even if it ignores established rules.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा ।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां शृणु
verses.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: The faith of the embodied is of three kinds, born of their own nature—Sattvic, Rajasic, and Tamasic. Hear now about it.

essence.reflection: Faith isn't all the same. It is colored by your personality (nature). You believe what you are.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सत्त्वानुरूपा सर्वस्य श्रद्धा भवति भारत ।
श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः
verses.english_translation: The faith of each is in accordance with his nature, O Bharata. The man consists of his faith; as a man's faith is, so is he.

essence.reflection: Your core beliefs define your reality. If your faith is pure, you are pure. If your faith is dull, you are dull.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यजन्ते सात्त्विका देवान्यक्षरक्षांसि राजसाः ।
प्रेतान्भूतगणांश्चान्ये यजन्ते तामसा जनाः
verses.english_translation: The Sattvic or pure men worship the gods; the Rajasic or passionate worship the Yakshas and Rakshasas; the others, the Tamasic people, worship the ghosts and the hosts of nature-spirits.

essence.reflection: The object of your attention reveals your inner quality. High minds seek the Divine; low minds seek power or dark spirits.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः ।
दम्भाहङ्कारसंयुक्ताः कामरागबलान्विताः
verses.english_translation: Those men who practice severe austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, impelled by the force of lust and attachment...

essence.reflection: Self-torture and extreme fasting done for show or ego are not spiritual. They are motivated by demonic pride.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
कर्षयन्तः शरीरस्थं भूतग्राममचेतसः ।
मां चैवान्तःशरीरस्थं तान्विद्ध्यासुरनिश्चयान्
verses.english_translation: ...Senselessly torturing all the elements in the body and Me also who dwell in the body—know thou these to be of demoniacal resolves.

essence.reflection: The body is the temple of God. Harming it in the name of spirituality disturbs the Divine dwelling within.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
आहारस्त्वपि सर्वस्य त्रिविधो भवति प्रियः ।
यज्ञस्तपस्तथा दानं तेषां भेदमिमं शृणु
verses.english_translation: The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.

essence.krishna_guidance: Know the three types of Food.
essence.reflection: What you eat affects how you think. Diet is the first step in spiritual discipline.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः ।
रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः
verses.english_translation: The foods which increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, and cheerfulness, which are savory and oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic people.

essence.reflection: Choose foods that nourish the body and calm the mind—fresh, juicy, and wholesome.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
कट्वम्ललवणात्युष्णतीक्ष्णरूक्षविदाहिनः ।
आहारा राजसस्येष्टा दुःखशोकामयप्रदाः
verses.english_translation: The foods that are bitter, sour, saline, excessively hot, pungent, dry, and burning are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief, and disease.

essence.reflection: Foods that overstimulate the senses (too spicy, too hot) lead to physical pain and mental agitation.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत् ।
उच्छिष्टमपि चामेध्यं भोजनं तामसप्रियम्
verses.english_translation: That which is stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten, and impure refuse, is the food liked by the Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Consuming dead, stale, or impure food dulls the consciousness and drains energy.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्यज्ञो विधिदृष्टो य इज्यते ।
यष्टव्यमेवेति मनः समाधाय स सात्त्विकः
verses.english_translation: That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for fruit, and as enjoined by ordinance, with a firm faith that it is their duty to offer, is Sattvic.

essence.reflection: Duty for duty's sake. Perform the ritual or good deed simply because it ought to be done, not for a reward.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अभिसन्धाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत् ।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम्
verses.english_translation: But that which is offered, O best of the Bharatas, with a view to reward and for ostentation, know it to be a Rajasic Yajna.

essence.reflection: Spiritual acts done for social status or material gain lose their purity. They are merely business transactions.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
विधिहीनमसृष्टान्नं मन्त्रहीनमदक्षिणम् ।
श्रद्धाविरहितं यज्ञं तामसं परिचक्षते
verses.english_translation: They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, which is devoid of Mantras and gifts, and which is devoid of faith.

essence.reflection: A chaotic, faithless ritual that helps no one (no food distributed) is an act of darkness.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
देवद्विजगुरुप्राज्ञपूजनं शौचमार्जवम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते
verses.english_translation: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the gurus, and the wise, purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, and non-injury are called the austerity of the body.

essence.reflection: Discipline starts with the body. Respect for elders, hygiene, and non-violence are physical forms of spiritual heat (Tapas).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् ।
स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते
verses.english_translation: Speech which causes no excitement, and is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial, and the practice of self-study (of Vedas)—these constitute the austerity of speech.

essence.reflection: Words have power. Use them to heal and help, not to disturb. Truth should be spoken kindly (Priyam).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मनःप्रसादः सौम्यत्वं मौनमात्मविनिग्रहः ।
भावसंशुद्धिरित्येतत्तपो मानसमुच्यते
verses.english_translation: Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, silence, self-control, purity of nature—this is called the mental austerity.

essence.reflection: Inner silence and cheerfulness are not accidents; they are disciplines of the mind.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
श्रद्धया परया तप्तं तपस्तत्त्रिविधं नरैः ।
अफलाकाङ्क्षिभिर्युक्तैः सात्त्विकं परिचक्षते
verses.english_translation: This threefold austerity, practiced by steadfast men with the utmost faith, desiring no fruit, they call Sattvic.

essence.reflection: When discipline of body, speech, and mind is done with faith and without a trade-off mentality, it is pure.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सत्कारमानपूजार्थं तपो दम्भेन चैव यत् ।
क्रियते तदिह प्रोक्तं राजसं चलमध्रुवम्
verses.english_translation: The austerity which is practiced with the object of gaining good reception, honor, and worship, and with hypocrisy, is said to be Rajasic, unstable, and transitory.

essence.reflection: Discipline done for 'likes' or reputation is unstable. It feeds the ego, not the soul.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मूढग्राहेणात्मनो यत्पीडया क्रियते तपः ।
परस्योत्सादनार्थं वा तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
verses.english_translation: That austerity which is practiced out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Suffering is not synonymous with holiness. Hurting oneself or others in the name of religion is darkness.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
दातव्यमिति यद्दानं दीयतेऽनुपकारिणे ।
देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्
verses.english_translation: That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that gift is held to be Sattvic.

essence.reflection: True charity is giving because it is right (Datavyam), to the right person, at the right time, expecting nothing back.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।
दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम्
verses.english_translation: And that gift which is given with a view to a return of the good, or looking for the fruit, or reluctantly, is held to be Rajasic.

essence.reflection: If you give with a heavy heart or expect a favor in return, it is a business transaction, not charity.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।
असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
verses.english_translation: The gift that is given at a wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult, is declared to be Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Throwing money at someone with contempt, or funding unworthy causes, is not charity; it is an act of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ॐ तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधः स्मृतः ।
ब्राह्मणास्तेन वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च विहिताः पुरा
verses.english_translation: 'Om Tat Sat'—this has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that were created formerly the Brahmanas, Vedas, and Sacrifices.

essence.krishna_guidance: Use the Mantra Om Tat Sat.
essence.reflection: This formula purifies all actions. 'Om' connects to the Source, 'Tat' signifies detachment, and 'Sat' signifies goodness and reality.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तस्मादोमित्युदाहृत्य यज्ञदानतपःक्रियाः ।
प्रवर्तन्ते विधानोक्ताः सततं ब्रह्मवादिनाम्
verses.english_translation: Therefore, with the utterance of 'Om', are the acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity as enjoined in the scriptures always begun by the students of Brahman.

essence.reflection: Invoking the Divine at the beginning of any good deed aligns the intent with the Universal Consciousness.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तदित्यनभिसन्धाय फलं यज्ञतपःक्रियाः ।
दानक्रियाश्च विविधाः क्रियन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षिभिः
verses.english_translation: Uttering 'Tat', without aiming at the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice and austerity and the various acts of gift performed by the seekers of liberation.

essence.reflection: 'Tat' reminds us that everything belongs to 'That' (the Divine). It helps in renouncing the sense of ownership.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सद्भावे साधुभावे च सदित्येतत्प्रयुज्यते ।
प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते
verses.english_translation: The word 'Sat' is used in the sense of Reality and of Goodness; and so also, O Partha, the word 'Sat' is used in the sense of an auspicious act.

essence.krishna_guidance: Use Sat for Truth and Goodness.
essence.reflection: Real existence (Satya) and Goodness are the same. What is true is good, and what is good is true.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते ।
कर्म चैव तदर्थीयं सदित्येवाभिधीयते
verses.english_translation: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and gift is also called 'Sat', and also action in connection with these (or for the sake of the Supreme) is called 'Sat'.

essence.reflection: Consistency in good deeds transforms them into a permanent spiritual asset.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत् ।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह
verses.english_translation: Whatever is sacrificed, given, or performed, and whatever austerity is practiced without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Partha; it is naught here or hereafter.

essence.reflection: Action without faith is a zero. It is 'Asat' (non-existent) because it lacks the spirit that gives it value in both this world and the next.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
संन्यासस्य महाबाहो तत्त्वमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ।
त्यागस्य च हृषीकेश पृथक्केशिनिषूदन
verses.english_translation: Arjuna said: I desire to know severally, O mighty-armed, the essence or truth of Renunciation (Sannyasa), O Hrishikesha, and of Abandonment (Tyaga), O slayer of Keshi.

essence.reflection: The spiritual journey ends where it began: understanding how to act (or not act) in the world. Distinguishing between 'giving up' and 'letting go' is crucial.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
काम्यानां कर्मणां न्यासं संन्यासं कवयो विदुः ।
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं प्राहुस्त्यागं विचक्षणाः
verses.english_translation: The Blessed Lord said: The sages understand Sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions as Tyaga.

essence.reflection: True renunciation isn't stopping work; it is stopping the desire behind the work (Sannyasa) and the demand for specific results (Tyaga).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
त्याज्यं दोषवदित्येके कर्म प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ।
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यमिति चापरे
verses.english_translation: Some philosophers declare that action should be abandoned as an evil; while others say that acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be abandoned.

essence.reflection: Blindly following philosophers causes confusion. One must discern which actions bind and which liberate.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
निश्चयं शृणु मे तत्र त्यागे भरतसत्तम ।
त्यागो हि पुरुषव्याघ्र त्रिविधः सम्प्रकीर्तितः
verses.english_translation: O best of the Bharatas, hear from Me the final truth about abandonment; for abandonment has been declared to be of three kinds, O tiger among men.

essence.reflection: When confused by opinions, rely on the Divine verdict. Krishna clarifies that abandonment is also subject to the Gunas.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यज्ञदानतपःकर्म न त्याज्यं कार्यमेव तत् ।
यज्ञो दानं तपश्चैव पावनानि मनीषिणाम्
verses.english_translation: Acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift, and austerity are the purifiers of the wise.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do not abandon Yajna, Dana, Tapas.
essence.reflection: Never give up self-improvement. Sacrifice, Charity, and Discipline act as soaps that scrub the mind clean.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
एतान्यपि तु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलानि च ।
कर्तव्यानीति मे पार्थ निश्चितं मतमुत्तमम्
verses.english_translation: But even these actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the fruits, O Partha; this is My certain and best belief.

essence.reflection: Do good works, but don't get addicted to being 'the doer' or 'the helper'. Detached service is the highest path.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
नियतस्य तु संन्यासः कर्मणो नोपपद्यते ।
मोहात्तस्य परित्यागस्तामसः परिकीर्तितः
verses.english_translation: Verily, the renunciation of obligatory duty is not proper; the abandonment of the same from delusion is declared to be Tamasic.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do not abandon duty out of Delusion (Moha).
essence.reflection: Running away from responsibility because you are confused or lazy is not spirituality; it is darkness (Tamas).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
दुःखमित्येव यत्कर्म कायक्लेशभयात्त्यजेत् ।
स कृत्वा राजसं त्यागं नैव त्यागफलं लभेत्
verses.english_translation: He who abandons action merely because it is difficult, or for fear of bodily trouble, he does not obtain the merit of renunciation by performing such Rajasic renunciation.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do not abandon duty out of Fear of Pain.
essence.reflection: Avoiding work because it is hard or uncomfortable is Rajasic. Comfort-seeking prevents spiritual growth.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
कार्यमित्येव यत्कर्म नियतं क्रियतेऽर्जुन ।
सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा फलकञ्चैव स त्यागः सात्त्विको मतः
verses.english_translation: Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the fruit, that abandonment is regarded as Sattvic.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do it because it Ought to be Done (Karyam).
essence.reflection: True renunciation is actually doing the work, but mentally renouncing the 'need' for it to pay off. This is Sattvic.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
न द्वेष्ट्यकुशलं कर्म कुशले नानुषज्जते ।
त्यागी सत्त्वसमाविष्टो मेधावी छिन्नसंशयः
verses.english_translation: The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate a disagreeable work nor is he attached to an agreeable one.

essence.reflection: A true Tyagi (Renouncer) doesn't pick and choose tasks based on preference. They do whatever life demands with equal poise.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
न हि देहभृता शक्यं त्यक्तुं कर्माण्यशेषतः ।
यस्तु कर्मफलत्यागी स त्यागीत्यभिधीयते
verses.english_translation: It is indeed impossible for an embodied being to renounce actions entirely. But he who renounces the fruit of action is said to be a man of renunciation.

essence.reflection: You have a body, so you must act. The only freedom available is the freedom from the anxiety of the result.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अनिष्टमिष्टं मिश्रं च त्रिविधं कर्मणः फलम् ।
भवत्यत्यागिनां प्रेत्य न तु संन्यासिनां क्वचित्
verses.english_translation: The threefold fruit of action—evil, good, and mixed—accrues after death to the non-renouncers, but never to those who have renounced.

essence.reflection: If you don't claim the work (via ego), you don't inherit the paycheck (karma). Renouncers are free from the cycle of reactions.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
पञ्चैतानि महाबाहो कारणानि निबोध मे ।
साङ्ख्ये कृतान्ते प्रोक्तानि सिद्धये सर्वकर्मणाम्
verses.english_translation: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed, these five causes for the accomplishment of all actions, as declared in the Sankhya system which is the end of all action.

essence.reflection: Success isn't just about 'You'. There are five factors involved in any action. Understanding this reduces ego.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अधिष्ठानं तथा कर्ता करणं च पृथग्विधम् ।
विविधाश्च पृथक्चेष्टा दैवं चैवात्र पञ्चमम्
verses.english_translation: The seat (body), the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various sorts, and the presiding deity (Destiny/Providence) as the fifth.

essence.reflection: The five factors are: Body, Doer, Instruments, Effort, and Destiny. You only control Effort. Destiny is the X-factor.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
शरीरवाङ्मनोभिर्यत्कर्म प्रारभते नरः ।
न्याय्यं वा विपरीतं वा पञ्चैते तस्य हेतवः
verses.english_translation: Whatever action a man performs with his body, speech, or mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.

essence.reflection: Every action, good or bad, is a collaboration of these five. No single individual is the sole cause of anything.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः ।
पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः
verses.english_translation: That being so, the man of perverse mind, who, on account of his untrained understanding, looks upon himself as the sole agent, he does not see.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do not think 'I am the Doer'.
essence.reflection: Thinking you are the sole cause of success or failure is the sign of an untrained mind (Akrta-buddhi). It creates unnecessary stress.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यस्य नाहङ्कृतो भावो बुद्धिर्यस्य न लिप्यते ।
हत्वापि स इमाँल्लोकान्न हन्ति न निबध्यते
verses.english_translation: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intellect is not tainted (by contact with objects), though he kills these people, he kills not, nor is he bound.

essence.reflection: This is the ultimate freedom. When the ego is gone, actions happen through you, not by you. Even drastic actions (like war) leave no karmic stain.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं परिज्ञाता त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ।
करणं कर्म कर्तेति त्रिविधः कर्मसङ्ग्रहः
verses.english_translation: Knowledge, the Object of Knowledge, and the Knower form the threefold impulse to action; the Organ, the Action, and the Agent form the threefold basis of action.

essence.reflection: Action starts in the mind (Knowledge/Knower) before it manifests in the world (Instrument/Doer). Watch the impulse to control the act.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ज्ञानं कर्म च कर्ता च त्रिधैव गुणभेदतः ।
प्रोच्यते गुणसङ्ख्याने यथावच्छृणु तान्यपि
verses.english_translation: Knowledge, action, and the agent are declared in the science of Gunas to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Hear them also duly.

essence.reflection: Everything in your life—your knowledge, your work, your personality—has a 'flavor' (Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas). Learn to identify it.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सर्वभूतेषु येनैकं भावमव्ययमीक्षते ।
अविभक्तं विभक्तेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि सात्त्विकम्
verses.english_translation: That by which the One Imperishable Being is seen in all beings, inseparate in the separated, know that knowledge to be Sattvic.

essence.reflection: Sattvic vision sees Unity in Diversity. It sees the one Life Force connecting all beings, despite their differences.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
पृथक्त्वेन तु यज्ज्ञानं नानाभावान्पृथग्विधान् ।
वेत्ति सर्वेषु भूतेषु तज्ज्ञानं विद्धि राजसम्
verses.english_translation: But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as different from one another, know that knowledge to be Rajasic.

essence.reflection: Rajasic vision sees only differences (race, species, status). It fragments the world and creates conflict.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यत्तु कृत्स्नवदेकस्मिन्कार्ये सक्तमहैतुकम् ।
अतत्त्वार्थवदल्पं च तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
verses.english_translation: But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without foundation in Truth, and trivial—that is declared to be Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Tamasic vision is fanaticism. It clings to one small idea or body as if it were the whole truth, ignoring reason.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
नियतं सङ्गरहितमरागद्वेषतः कृतम् ।
अफलप्रेप्सुना कर्म यत्तत्सात्त्विकमुच्यते
verses.english_translation: An action which is ordained, which is free from attachment, which is done without love or hatred by one who is not desirous of any fruit—that is declared to be Sattvic.

essence.reflection: The perfect act is Duty done without Drama (love/hate) and without Demand (fruit).

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यत्तु कामेप्सुना कर्म साहङ्कारेण वा पुनः ।
क्रियते बहुलायासं तद्राजसमुदाहृतम्
verses.english_translation: But that action which is done by one longing for desires, or again with egoism, or with much effort, is declared to be Rajasic.

essence.reflection: If your work feels like a 'grind' (Bahulayasam) and is driven by ego, it is Rajasic. It leads to burnout.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अनुबन्धं क्षयं हिंसामनपेक्ष्य च पौरुषम् ।
मोहादारभ्यते कर्म यत्तत्तामसमुच्यते
verses.english_translation: That action which is undertaken from delusion, without regard for the consequences, loss, injury, and one's own ability—that is declared to be Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Acting blindly without considering the cost or the harm it causes to others is the mark of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते
verses.english_translation: An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is called Sattvic.

essence.reflection: The ideal worker has enthusiasm (Utsaha) but no ego. They keep working cheerfully whether they win or lose.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
रागी कर्मफलप्रेप्सुर्लुब्धो हिंसात्मकोऽशुचिः ।
हर्षशोकान्वितः कर्ता राजसः परिकीर्तितः
verses.english_translation: Passionate, desiring to obtain the fruit of action, greedy, harmful, impure, moved by joy and sorrow—such an agent is said to be Rajasic.

essence.reflection: Being an emotional roller-coaster (Joy/Sorrow), greedy, and cruel makes one a slave to their own passions.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अयुक्तः प्राकृतः स्तब्धः शठो नैष्कृतिकोऽलसः ।
विषादी दीर्घसूत्री च कर्ता तामस उच्यते
verses.english_translation: Unsteady, vulgar, stubborn, deceitful, malicious, indolent, despondent, and procrastinating—such an agent is called Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Procrastination (Dirghasutri) and chronic depression (Vishadi) are signs of Tamas. Wake up and act.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
बुद्धेर्भेदं धृतेश्चैव गुणतस्त्रिविधं शृणु ।
प्रोच्यमानमशेषेण पृथक्त्वेन धनञ्जय
verses.english_translation: Hear the threefold division of intellect and firmness, according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Dhananjaya.

essence.reflection: Your capacity to understand (Intellect) and your capacity to stick to a goal (Will) also have qualities. Check them.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कार्याकार्ये भयाभये ।
बन्धं मोक्षं च या वेत्ति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी
verses.english_translation: That which knows the path of work and renunciation, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation—that intellect is Sattvic, O Partha.

essence.reflection: True intelligence isn't IQ; it's the ability to distinguish between what binds you and what frees you.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यया धर्ममधर्मं च कार्यं चाकार्यमेव च ।
अयथावत्प्रजानाति बुद्धिः सा पार्थ राजसी
verses.english_translation: That by which one incorrectly understands Dharma and Adharma, and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done—that intellect, O Partha, is Rajasic.

essence.reflection: A confused moral compass leads to gray areas where right and wrong are blurred by desire.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अधर्मं धर्ममिति या मन्यते तमसावृता ।
सर्वार्थान्विपरीतांश्च बुद्धिः सा पार्थ तामसी
verses.english_translation: That which, enveloped in darkness, sees Adharma as Dharma and all things in a perverted light, that intellect, O Partha, is Tamasic.

essence.reflection: The inverted mind sees bad as good and good as bad. This perversion of truth is the hallmark of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
धृत्या यया धारयते मनःप्राणेन्द्रियक्रियाः ।
योगेनाव्यभिचारिण्या धृतिः सा पार्थ सात्त्विकी
verses.english_translation: The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, one holds fast the functions of the mind, the life-breath, and the senses, that firmness, O Partha, is Sattvic.

essence.reflection: Willpower isn't just grit; it's the steady, yoga-aligned focus that keeps the mind and senses on track.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यया तु धर्मकामार्थान्धृत्या धारयतेऽर्जुन ।
प्रसङ्गेन फलाकाङ्क्षी धृतिः सा पार्थ राजसी
verses.english_translation: But the firmness, O Arjuna, by which one holds fast to Dharma, pleasure, and wealth, desirous of the fruit of each from attachment, that firmness, O Partha, is Rajasic.

essence.reflection: Being stubborn about worldly goals (money, pleasure) is not true strength; it is just obsession.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यया स्वप्नं भयं शोकं विषादं मदमेव च ।
न विमुञ्चति दुर्मेधा धृतिः सा पार्थ तामसी
verses.english_translation: That by which a stupid man does not give up sleep, fear, grief, despair, and also arrogance—that firmness, O Partha, is Tamasic.

essence.reflection: Holding onto depression, fear, or laziness with a stubborn grip is Tamasic determination. Learn to let go.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सुखं त्विदानीं त्रिविधं शृणु मे भरतर्षभ ।
अभ्यासाद्रमते यत्र दुःखान्तं च निगच्छति
verses.english_translation: And now hear from Me, O best of the Bharatas, of the threefold happiness. That in which one rejoices by long practice and in which one comes to the end of pain...

essence.reflection: True happiness isn't instant; it comes from practice (Abhyasa) and leads to the permanent end of sorrow.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यत्तदग्रे विषमिव परिणामेऽमृतोपमम् ।
तत्सुखं सात्त्विकं प्रोक्तमात्मबुद्धिप्रसादजम्
verses.english_translation: ...Which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar—that happiness is declared to be Sattvic, born of the purity of one's own intellect.

essence.reflection: Discipline feels like poison (hard work) in the beginning but tastes like nectar (success/peace) in the end. Endure the start.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
विषयेन्द्रियसंयोगाद्यत्तदग्रेऽमृतोपमम् ।
परिणामे विषमिव तत्सुखं राजसं स्मृतम्
verses.english_translation: That happiness which arises from the contact of the sense-organs with the objects, which is at first like nectar, and in the end like poison—that is declared to be Rajasic.

essence.reflection: Sensory pleasure feels great instantly (nectar) but leads to addiction and pain (poison) later. Don't be fooled by the start.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यदग्रे चानुबन्धे च सुखं मोहनमात्मनः ।
निद्रालस्यप्रमादोत्थं तत्तामसमुदाहृतम्
verses.english_translation: That happiness which begins and results in self-delusion, arising from sleep, indolence, and heedlessness—that is declared to be Tamasic.

essence.reflection: The comfort of sleep or laziness is a trap. It deludes the soul from start to finish.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः ।
सत्त्वं प्रकृतिजैर्मुक्तं यदेभिः स्यात्त्रिभिर्गुणैः
verses.english_translation: There is no being on earth, or again in heaven among the gods, that is liberated from the three qualities born of Nature.

essence.krishna_guidance: Know the reach of the Gunas.
essence.reflection: Everyone and everything is colored by these three qualities. Only the liberated soul is free from them.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां शूद्राणां च परन्तप ।
कर्माणि प्रविभक्तानि स्वभावप्रभवैर्गुणैः
verses.english_translation: Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas, as also of Sudras, O Parantapa, the duties are distributed according to the qualities born of their own nature.

essence.reflection: Social roles are based on natural aptitudes (Gunas), not just birth. Find the work that matches your inner nature.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
शमो दमस्तपः शौचं क्षान्तिरार्जवमेव च ।
ज्ञानं विज्ञानमास्तिक्यं ब्रह्मकर्म स्वभावजम्
verses.english_translation: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, and also uprightness, knowledge, realization, and belief in God—these are the duties of the Brahmanas, born of (their own) nature.

essence.reflection: These are the qualities of the intellectual/spiritual class: Peace, discipline, and wisdom.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
शौर्यं तेजो धृतिर्दाक्ष्यं युद्धे चाप्यपलायनम् ।
दानमीश्वरभावश्च क्षात्रं कर्म स्वभावजम्
verses.english_translation: Prowess, splendor, firmness, dexterity, and also not fleeing from battle, generosity, and lordliness—these are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of (their own) nature.

essence.reflection: Leadership requires courage, resilience, and generosity. Don't run from the battle of life.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
कृषिगौरक्ष्यवाणिज्यं वैश्यकर्म स्वभावजम् ।
परिचर्यात्मकं कर्म शूद्रस्यापि स्वभावजम्
verses.english_translation: Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade are the duties of the Vaishya, born of (his own) nature; and action consisting of service is the duty of the Sudra, born of (his own) nature.

essence.reflection: Whether commerce or service, every role sustains society. All work is dignified if it matches your nature.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यभिरतः संसिद्धिं लभते नरः ।
स्वकर्मनिरतः सिद्धिं यथा विन्दति तच्छृणु
verses.english_translation: Each man, devoted to his own duty, attains perfection. How he attains perfection while engaged in his own duty, hear now.

essence.reflection: You don't need to change your job to find God. You can find perfection right where you are, by doing your specific duty perfectly.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यतः प्रवृत्तिर्भूतानां येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
स्वकर्मणा तमभ्यर्च्य सिद्धिं विन्दति मानवः
verses.english_translation: He from whom is the evolution of all beings, by whom all this is pervaded, worshipping Him with his own duty, a man attains perfection.

essence.reflection: Turn your daily job into a Puja. If you offer your work to the Source of all beings, the work itself becomes the path to liberation.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् ।
स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्
verses.english_translation: Better is one's own duty (though) destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.

essence.reflection: It is better to be an imperfect 'You' than a perfect 'Someone Else'. Authenticity is spiritual protection.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सहजं कर्म कौन्तेय सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् ।
सर्वारम्भा हि दोषेण धूमेनाग्निरिवावृताः
verses.english_translation: One should not abandon, O Kaunteya, the duty to which one is born, though faulty; for all undertakings are enveloped by evil, as fire by smoke.

essence.reflection: Nothing in the material world is perfect. Every job has a downside. Don't quit just because it's difficult or imperfect; stick to your nature.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
असक्तबुद्धिः सर्वत्र जितात्मा विगतस्पृहः ।
नैष्कर्म्यसिद्धिं परमां संन्यासेनाधिगच्छति
verses.english_translation: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, whose desire has fled, he by renunciation attains the supreme state of freedom from action.

essence.reflection: By detaching from the world and mastering the self, one reaches a state where actions no longer leave a mark on the soul.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सिद्धिं प्राप्तो यथा ब्रह्म तथाप्नोति निबोध मे ।
समासेनैव कौन्तेय निष्ठा ज्ञानस्य या परा
verses.english_translation: Learn from Me in brief, O Kaunteya, how he who has attained perfection reaches Brahman, that supreme consummation of knowledge.

essence.reflection: Krishna summarizes the final steps to the highest realization. Pay attention.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
बुद्ध्या विशुद्धया युक्तो धृत्यात्मानं नियम्य च ।
शब्दादीन्विषयांस्त्यक्त्वा रागद्वेषौ व्युदस्य च
verses.english_translation: Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self with firmness, rejecting sound and other objects, and abandoning attraction and hatred...

essence.reflection: The toolkit for liberation: Pure Intellect, Firm Will, and rejection of sensory distractions and emotional extremes.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
विविक्तसेवी लघ्वाशी यतवाक्कायमानसः ।
ध्यानयोगपरो नित्यं वैराग्यं समुपाश्रितः
verses.english_translation: ...Dwelling in solitude, eating but little, speech, body, and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, taking refuge in dispassion...

essence.reflection: Solitude, light eating, and silence are the external aids. Meditation and dispassion are the internal engines.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अहङ्कारं बलं दर्प कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ।
विमुच्य निर्ममः शान्तो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते
verses.english_translation: ...Having abandoned egoism, power, arrogance, desire, anger, and covetousness, destitute of the notion of 'mine' and peaceful, he is fit for becoming Brahman.

essence.reflection: You must drop the heavy baggage of Ego, Power, and Anger to enter the subtle realm of the Spirit.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ब्रह्मभूतः प्रसन्नात्मा न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ।
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मद्भक्तिं लभते पराम्
verses.english_translation: Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires; the same to all beings, he obtains supreme devotion to Me.

essence.reflection: Realization (Brahma-bhuta) isn't the end; it leads to the highest form of Devotion. A happy soul naturally loves God.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः ।
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम्
verses.english_translation: By devotion he knows Me in truth, what and who I am; then having known Me in truth, he forthwith enters into the Supreme.

essence.krishna_guidance: Know and Enter Me through Bhakti.
essence.reflection: Love is the only way to fully know the Beloved. Knowledge allows you to see the door; Love opens it.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्यपाश्रयः ।
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम्
verses.english_translation: Doing all actions always, taking refuge in Me, by My grace he obtains the eternal, indestructible State.

essence.reflection: You can do any work. If you take refuge in the Divine, His Grace guarantees your destination.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः ।
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव
verses.english_translation: Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, resorting to the Yoga of discrimination, do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.

essence.reflection: Keep your hands busy with work, but keep your mind busy with God. Use your intellect to maintain this connection.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मच्चिततः सर्वदुर्गाणि मत्प्रसादात्तरिष्यसि ।
अथ चेत्त्वमहङ्कारान्न श्रोष्यसि विनङ्क्ष्यसि
verses.english_translation: Fixing thy mind on Me, thou shalt by My grace cross over all difficulties; but if from egoism thou wilt not hear (Me), thou shalt perish.

essence.krishna_guidance: Cross all Obstacles. Warning: Don't use Ego.
essence.reflection: With God, you are invincible. Without God (in ego), you are vulnerable. The choice is yours: Grace or Ruin.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यदहङ्कारमाश्रित्य न योत्स्य इति मन्यसे ।
मिथ्यैष व्यवसायस्ते प्रकृतिस्त्वां नियोक्ष्यति
verses.english_translation: Having taken refuge in egoism, thou thinkest 'I will not fight'; vain is this thy resolve; Nature will impel thee.

essence.reflection: You cannot fake non-violence. If you are a warrior by nature, you will fight eventually. Don't let ego dictate impossible vows.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
स्वभावजेन कौन्तेय निबद्धः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
कर्तुं नेच्छसि यन्मोहात्करिष्यस्यवशोऽपि तत्
verses.english_translation: Bound by thy own duty born of nature, O son of Kunti, that which from delusion thou desirest not to do, even that thou shalt do helplessly.

essence.reflection: It is better to do your duty willingly and offer it to God than to be dragged into it kicking and screaming by destiny.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।
भ्रामयन्सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया
verses.english_translation: The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusive power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.

essence.reflection: We are like puppets on a machine (the body), driven by the Inner Controller. Realize who is pulling the strings.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तमेव शरणं गच्छ सर्वभावेन भारत ।
तत्प्रसादात्परां शान्तिं स्थानं प्राप्स्यसि शाश्वतम्
verses.english_translation: Fly unto Him for refuge with all thy being, O Bharata; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

essence.reflection: Surrender completely to that Inner Ruler. His grace is the only way to find the eternal peace you seek.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
इति ते ज्ञानमाख्यातं गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं मया ।
विमृश्यैतदशेषेण यथेच्छसि तथा कुरु
verses.english_translation: Thus has wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected on it fully, then act as thou wishest.

essence.krishna_guidance: Do as you wish (Yathecchasi tatha kuru).
essence.reflection: God respects free will. He gives the knowledge, but the final choice to act is yours. Reflect and choose wisely.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम्
verses.english_translation: Hear again My supreme word, most secret of all; because thou art dearly loved of Me, therefore I will tell thee what is good.

essence.reflection: Krishna shares the final secret not because of rules, but because of Love. You are dear to the Divine.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे
verses.english_translation: Fix thy mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. Thou shalt come even to Me; truly do I promise unto thee, (for) thou art dear to Me.

essence.reflection: God gives His word. If you devote yourself to Him, He guarantees your liberation. You are His beloved.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः
verses.english_translation: Abandoning all duties, take refuge in Me alone; I will liberate thee from all sins; grieve not.

essence.reflection: The Charama Shloka: Drop all other strategies, rituals, and dependencies. Rely solely on God. He takes care of the rest.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति
verses.english_translation: This is never to be spoken by thee to one who is devoid of austerity, to one who is not devoted, nor to one who does not render service, nor who does not desire to listen, nor to one who speaks ill of Me.

essence.reflection: Don't cast pearls before swine. Share this wisdom only with those who are ready, respectful, and willing to listen.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
य इदं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः
verses.english_translation: He who with supreme devotion to Me will teach this supreme secret to My devotees, shall doubtless come to Me.

essence.reflection: Sharing spiritual wisdom is the highest service to God. It ensures your own union with the Divine.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि
verses.english_translation: Nor is there any among men who does dearer service to Me, nor shall there be another on earth dearer to Me than he.

essence.krishna_guidance: Be My Dearest. Share the Gita.
essence.reflection: To be loved by God, love His children enough to share the truth with them. The teacher of wisdom is the most beloved.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः
verses.english_translation: And he who will study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall have been worshipped by the sacrifice of wisdom; such is My conviction.

essence.reflection: Just reading and thinking about the Gita is a form of worship (Jnana Yajna). Intellectual engagement is spiritual practice.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम्
verses.english_translation: The man also who hears this, full of faith and free from malice, he too, liberated, shall attain to the happy worlds of those of righteous deeds.

essence.reflection: Even passive listening with a good heart brings immense merit and freedom from sin.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।
कच्चिदज्ञानसम्मोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय
verses.english_translation: Has this been heard, O son of Pritha, with one-pointed mind? Has the delusion of thy ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?

essence.reflection: Krishna checks if the teaching worked. The goal was not just to speak, but to remove Arjuna's confusion.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
अर्जुन उवाच ।
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव
verses.english_translation: Arjuna said: Destroyed is my delusion as I have gained my memory (knowledge) through Thy grace, O Achyuta. I am firm, my doubts are gone. I will act according to Thy word.

essence.reflection: Karishye Vachanam Tava (I will do Your bidding). This is the ideal state of a disciple—delusion gone, doubts cleared, ready to act.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
सञ्जय उवाच ।
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।
संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम्
verses.english_translation: Sanjaya said: Thus have I heard this wonderful dialogue between Vasudeva and the high-souled Partha, which causes the hair to stand on end.

essence.reflection: The teaching is so powerful it causes physical symptoms of awe (Romaharshanam) in the listener.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् ।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम्
verses.english_translation: Through the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this supreme and most secret Yoga directly from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, Himself declaring it.

essence.reflection: Gratitude for the teacher (Vyasa) who enables us to hear the Divine message.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।
केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः
verses.english_translation: O King, remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

essence.reflection: Spiritual truth is a source of endless joy. Remembering it (Samsmritya) keeps the inspiration alive.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन्हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः
verses.english_translation: And remembering again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, great is my amazement, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

essence.reflection: The vision of the Cosmic Form remains etched in the mind, a constant source of wonder and joy.

verses.sanskrit_verse:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम
verses.english_translation: Wherever there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and wherever there is Partha, the wielder of the bow, there are prosperity, victory, expansion, and sound policy; such is my conviction.

essence.reflection: Victory is guaranteed when Divine Grace (Krishna) is combined with Human Effort (Arjuna). This is the formula for success in life.
